depth_justification: Questions and risks do name this app's concrete choices (EfficientNet-B4 on ISIC 2020, the dermatoscopic-vs-smartphone capture gap, Platt calibration, Fitzpatrick I-III bias, missing Grad-CAM), but almost every specific was surfaced by the developer first and merely echoed back with a fixed 'how does this align with the EU AI Act' suffix; the copilot reuses the same dimension tag (P3.D10) across unrelated risks and its article citations are loose or misattributed ('EU AI Act Art. 38/35/34/39' for transparency/robustness/fairness/accountability), keeping it templated rather than laser-focused.
actionability_justification: Mitigations stay directional rather than implementable ('Implement GDPR-compliant erasure workflows', 'Use stronger anonymization techniques where possible', 'Conduct fairness audits and adjust model training', 'Implement real-time monitoring') with no thresholds, data flows, UI specs, or correct article hooks; nearly the entire dialogue is questions back to the developer rather than advice, so a developer could not build from this tomorrow.
salient_examples: What specific measures are you implementing to ensure that the pseudonymization of patient data meets the GDPR standard of "adequate security" and prevents re-identification, especially when the data is used for retraining the CNN model? [P2.D3] (a near-verbatim repeat of the prior turn)
Mitigation: Use stronger anonymization techniques where possible, and document pseudonymization methods. Reference: GDPR Art. 4(11).
Mitigation: Conduct fairness audits and adjust model training to include diverse skin types. Reference: EU AI Act Art. 34 (Fairness).
